mainTopic: The end of רבי בנאה's corrections of the inscriptions, the measures at קפוטקיא, and a new משנה on חזקה for spouts, gutter pipes, ladders and windows, with three explanations of the מרזב rule.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of the story of רבי בנאה, who corrects badly worded inscriptions written by the wise men of the nations. First he fixes the rule about judges: a judge is disqualified only if the court actually takes money from him, not just because he was sued. Next he fixes the line about blood and wine: blood is the head of all illness, not all death, and wine is the head of all healing, not all life. Each time, the writers add his wording in the name of 'the elders of the Jews.' The גמרא then notes three measure names written at the gate of קפוטקיא and explains that אנטל is the רביעית of the תורה. A new משנה follows. It covers when a person gains a חזקה (a lasting right) for a roof spout (מרזב), a gutter pipe (מזחילה), ladders, and windows, and רבי יהודה adds that a framed window counts even if it is small. The גמרא then gives three explanations of how a מרזב can have no חזקה while its place does: שמואל, רבי חנינא, and רב ירמיה בר אבא.

steps.title: Anyone could disqualify a judge just by suing him
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה challenges the inscription that says any judge who is called to court is no longer a judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if someone summons him to court, has he disqualified him?!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the story in the middle. רבי בנאה is attacking an inscription that said any judge called to court is not a real judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being called to court were enough to disqualify a judge, any troublemaker could remove a judge just by filing a lawsuit against him. Being summoned proves nothing, because the judge might be found innocent.

phrases.english: and someone summons him to judgment,
phrases.notes: Some versions say לְהוּ ('them'); the corrected wording in square brackets says לֵיהּ ('him'), meaning the judge.

phrases.english: has he disqualified him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי בנאה's challenge from the previous part of the דף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inscription 'any judge who is called to court is not a judge.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being summoned is not proof of guilt, so the rule as written would let anyone disqualify a judge.

steps.title: The correct wording: only a judge who loses the case
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה gives the proper wording: a judge is disqualified only if money is actually taken from him by a court ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it should say: any judge who is called to court, and money is lawfully taken from him, is not called a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה fixes the inscription by adding one condition: the judge must actually lose the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with the old wording was that it punished a judge just for being sued. The new wording adds 'and money is taken from him by law,' so only a judge proven to have taken what was not his is disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: they take money out of his hands

phrases.english: Rather, any judge who is called to court,
and money is taken from him by law,
is not called a judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 1 by fixing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being called to court alone disqualifies a judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a judge whom the court actually orders to pay is disqualified.

steps.title: The writers add the corrected judge rule
steps.stepSummary: The writers accept רבי בנאה's fix and add it to the inscription in the name of 'the elders of the Jews.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They wrote this: 'But the elders of the Jews say: any judge who is called to court and money is lawfully taken from him is not called a judge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The people who wrote the inscription agree with רבי בנאה and add his correct version underneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They do not erase the old line. They add a note starting with 'But the elders of the Jews say,' which shows that the Jewish sages' wording is the more exact one.
steps.whatToRemember: A judge is not disqualified just because he was sued. He is disqualified only if the court actually makes him pay.

phrases.english: They wrote this:
'But the elders of the Jews say:
any judge who is called to court
and money is taken from him by law
is not called a judge.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַבוּ הָכִי: בְּרַם סָאבֵי דִיהוּדָאֵי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי בנאה's correction was accepted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The corrected rule is written into the inscription: only a judge who actually loses the case is disqualified.

steps.title: A second inscription about blood and wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה sees another inscription: blood is at the head of all death, and wine is at the head of all life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw that it was written: 'At the head of all death am I, blood; at the head of all life am I, wine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a second inscription that רבי בנאה read. This sets up his next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inscription makes two big claims. Too much blood is the main cause of every death, and wine is the main source of every life.

keyTerms.meaning: at the head of, first of

phrases.english: He saw that it was written:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי בנאה, still reading the inscriptions.

phrases.english: 'At the head of all death am I, blood;
at the head of all life am I, wine.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new inscription after the judge inscription was settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inscription: blood causes all death, and wine gives all life.

steps.title: Not every death comes from blood, and wine cannot save everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה gives two examples that show the inscription is too broad.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, someone who falls from a roof and dies, or falls from a palm tree and dies, was it blood that killed him?! And also, if someone is about to die, can they give him wine to drink and he will live?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה attacks both halves of the inscription with examples from real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, a person who dies from a fall did not die because of blood, so blood is not 'the head of all death.' Second, wine cannot bring a dying person back to life, so wine is not 'the head of all life.'

keyTerms.meaning: if that is so, then (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: If that is so,
one who falls from a roof and dies,
or one who falls from a palm tree and dies,
did blood kill him?!
And furthermore, someone who is on his way to dying,
they give him wine to drink, and he lives?!

steps.kashyaTarget: Both halves of the blood-and-wine inscription.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real cases show that some deaths have nothing to do with blood, and wine cannot save a dying person.

steps.title: Correct wording: illness and healing, not death and life
steps.stepSummary: רבי בנאה suggests saying blood is the head of all illness, and wine is the head of all healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what should be written: 'At the head of all illness am I, blood; at the head of all healing am I, wine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי בנאה fixes the inscription by changing two words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He changes 'death' to 'illness' and 'life' to 'healing.' Now the claims fit his examples: blood causes many sicknesses, not every death, and wine helps cure, but it does not bring back the dying.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what should be written:
At the head of all illness am I, blood;
at the head of all healing am I, wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by fixing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood causes all death and wine gives all life.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood is the main cause of illness and wine is the main healer.

steps.title: The writers add the corrected blood-and-wine line
steps.stepSummary: The writers accept the fix, credit 'the elders of the Jews,' and add that where there is no wine, medicines are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They wrote this: 'But the elders of the Jews say: At the head of all illness am I, blood; at the head of all healing am I, wine. In a place where there is no wine, there medicines are needed.'
steps.whatsHappening: Again the writers accept רבי בנאה's correction and add it to the inscription, with one extra line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra line is 'where there is no wine, medicines are needed.' It stresses how much wine helps heal: without it, people have to turn to other medicines.
steps.whatToRemember: Both inscriptions were too broad. רבי בנאה made them exact, and the writers added his wording as 'the elders of the Jews say.'

phrases.english: They wrote this:
'But the elders of the Jews say:
At the head of all illness am I, blood;
at the head of all healing am I, wine;
in a place where there is no wine,
there medicines are needed.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַבוּ הָכִי: בְּרַם סָאבֵי דִיהוּדָאֵי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the correction in step 6 was accepted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The inscription is corrected: blood is the head of illness, wine is the head of healing, and without wine people need medicines.

steps.title: Measurement names written at the gate of קפוטקיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports three words written at the entrance of קפוטקיא: אנפק, אנבג, אנטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was written at the entrance of קפוטקיא: 'אנפק, אנבג, אנטל.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the story was about writings on walls, the גמרא adds another one: three names for measures written at a city gate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three words are names of measures used in קפוטקיא. The next step asks which Torah measure one of them equals.

phrases.english: It was written at the entrance of קפוטקיא:
'אנפק, אנבג, אנטל.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side note connected to the theme of inscriptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three measure names were written at the entrance of קפוטקיא.

steps.title: Which measure is the אנטל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word אנטל means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of one of the three words. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks what this foreign measure equals in measures we know.

phrases.english: And what is אנטל?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the inscription in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of the measure called אנטל.

steps.title: אנטל is the תורה's רביעית
steps.stepSummary: The answer: אנטל is the רביעית of the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the רביעית of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אנטל equals a רביעית, the quarter-לוג measure used in the laws of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the foreign word on the gate stands for a measure we already know from הלכה: the רביעית, a quarter of a לוג.

keyTerms.meaning: a quarter of a לוג, a liquid measure
of the Torah, used in Torah law

phrases.english: It is the quarter of the Torah.
phrases.notes: He means a רביעית, a quarter of a לוג, the measure used in many הלכות.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אנטל equals the Torah's רביעית (a quarter-לוג).

steps.title: New משנה: rights for a roof spout and a gutter pipe
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a מרזב has no חזקה but its place does, and a מזחילה has a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A spout has no חזקה, but its place has a חזקה. A gutter pipe has a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about water draining from one person's roof toward a neighbor's property. It tells us when a person gains a lasting right (חזקה) to keep it there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מרזב is a short spout that sticks out from the roof. Its owner gets no חזקה for the spout itself, but he does get one for its place. A מזחילה is a gutter pipe running along the roof, and its owner does gain a חזקה for it. The גמרא will explain the details.

keyTerms.meaning: a short spout from a roof gutter
a right gained by using something over time
a gutter pipe running along the roof

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין לו חזקה' does not mean the spout has nothing to do with חזקה at all. Its place still gets a חזקה. Only the spout itself does not, as the גמרא will explain.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A spout has no acquired right,
but its place has an acquired right.
A gutter pipe has an acquired right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מרזב has no חזקה, but its place does. A מזחילה has a חזקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה starts a new discussion about which uses of a neighbor's property create a lasting legal right.

steps.title: A small ladder gives no right, a fixed ladder does
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that an Egyptian ladder has no חזקה and a Tyrian ladder does.
steps.simpleTranslation: An Egyptian ladder has no חזקה, but a Tyrian ladder does have a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of things that can or cannot create a חזקה, an established right. Now it talks about ladders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סולם המצרי is small and easy to carry, so leaning it somewhere does not set up a lasting right. A סולם הצורי is big and stays in one place, so using it over time does create a חזקה. The rule depends on whether the object is temporary or permanent.

keyTerms.meaning: An Egyptian ladder: small and portable
An established right built up through use over time

phrases.english: An Egyptian ladder has no established right,
phrases.notes: An Egyptian ladder is a small one you can pick up and move.

phrases.english: but a Tyrian one does have an established right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list after the מרזב and מזחילה cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A portable ladder creates no חזקה; a large, fixed ladder does.

steps.title: A small window gives no right, a large window does
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on Egyptian and Tyrian windows and defines an Egyptian window as one too small for a head to enter.
steps.simpleTranslation: An Egyptian window has no חזקה, but a Tyrian window does. What is an Egyptian window? Any window that a person's head cannot fit into.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the same kind of rule for windows. Then it explains exactly which window counts as the small 'Egyptian' kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large window creates a חזקה, but a small one does not. The משנה gives a clear test for 'small': if a person cannot put his head through it, it is an Egyptian window.

keyTerms.meaning: An Egyptian window: a small window
Which is it? A phrase the משנה uses to introduce a definition

phrases.english: An Egyptian window has no established right,
but a Tyrian one does have an established right.
Which is an Egyptian window?
Any window that a person's head
is not able to enter into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same small-versus-large pattern from ladders to windows and adds a definition
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A window too small for a head to enter creates no חזקה; a larger window does.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a framed window counts even if small
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that a window with a frame creates a חזקה even if a head cannot fit through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if the window has a frame, then even if a person's head cannot fit into it, it has a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a second way a window can create a חזקה. In his view, a frame is enough even if the window is small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion looks only at size. רבי יהודה says a frame (מלבן) shows the window was made to be permanent. So a framed window creates a חזקה even when it fails the head test.

keyTerms.meaning: A frame built around a window

steps.whatToRemember: For windows, the first opinion uses only the head-size test. רבי יהודה also accepts a frame as a sign that the window is permanent.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If it has a frame,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
phrases.english: even though a person's head
is not able to enter into it,
this is an established right.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם יֵשׁ לָהּ מַלְבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the definition just given by adding a frame as another qualifying feature
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A framed window creates a חזקה regardless of size.

steps.title: What does the מרזב rule mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by saying a מרזב has no חזקה but its place does.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does it mean that a spout has no חזקה, but its place does have a חזקה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes back to the first line of the משנה (step 11). It asks what that confusing line means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line seems to contradict itself. If the spout has no חזקה, how can its place have one? The גמרא wants to know what is fixed and what is not.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
A spout that drains water off a roof
To its place (where the water lands or the spout sits)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is meant by 'A spout has no established right,'
but its place has an established right'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the end of the משנה and returns to its opening line
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a spout can lack a חזקה while its place has one

steps.title: שמואל: the spout can be moved along one side, not to another side
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains: no חזקה on one side, but a חזקה between two sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: this is what it means. The spout has no חזקה on one side, but its place has a חזקה between two sides.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question from step 15. The neighbor can move the spout along the same side of the roof, but he cannot move it to a different side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No חזקה' means the exact spot along one wall is not fixed. 'Its place has a חזקה' means the side of the roof the water drains from is fixed. So the two halves of the line talk about different things and do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (introduces an explanation)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּרְזֵב אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה – מֵרוּחַ אַחַת,
phrases.english: The spout has no established right on one side,
phrases.notes: He means the neighbor may shift the spout to another spot along the same side of the roof.

phrases.english: but its place has an established right between two sides.
phrases.notes: He means the neighbor may not move it to a different side of the roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the מרזב line
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The spout can be moved along one side, but it cannot be moved to a different side.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: a long spout can be shortened but not removed
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains: 'no חזקה' means a long spout may be shortened, and 'its place has a חזקה' means it may not be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: the spout has no חזקה, meaning that if it is long, the neighbor may shorten it. Its place has a חזקה, meaning that if he comes to remove it, he may not remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives a different explanation of the same משנה line. He reads 'no חזקה' as being about the spout's length, and 'its place' as being about the spout's right to exist at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the question is where along the roof the spout sits. For רבי חנינא, the question is how long the spout is. A long spout can be cut down, but the right to have a spout there is fixed, so the neighbor cannot take it away completely.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of 'the spout has no חזקה but its place does.' שמואל: it can be moved along one side but not to another side. רבי חנינא: it can be shortened but not removed.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא is not adding to שמואל. He gives a separate explanation of what 'no חזקה' means.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
The spout has no established right,
meaning that if it was long, he may shorten it,
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the neighbor below, whose property gets the water.

phrases.english: but its place has an established right,
meaning that if he comes to remove it, he may not remove it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: הַמַּרְזֵב אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the question in step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The spout's length is not protected, but the right to have it there is protected, so it cannot be removed.

steps.title: רב ירמיה בר אבא: you may build under the spout but not remove it
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא gives a third explanation of the משנה. 'No חזקה' means the neighbor may build under the spout. 'Its place has a חזקה' means he may not uproot the spout entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: The spout has no חזקה, meaning that if the neighbor wants to build underneath it, he may build. But its place does have a חזקה, meaning that if he comes to remove it, he may not remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer to the question from step 15 about what the משנה's words on the מרזב mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא (step 17) said the neighbor may shorten a long spout but not remove it. רב ירמיה בר אבא agrees the spout itself can never be removed. But his example of what the neighbor may do is different: the neighbor may build a structure under the spout, and the spout owner cannot stop him.

keyTerms.meaning: A rain spout that sends water off a roof into the neighbor's yard
A right gained by using something for a long time without protest
To build underneath it (under the spout)
Its place, meaning the very spot where the spout is fixed
To uproot it, to remove it completely

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of 'the מרזב has no חזקה, but its place has a חזקה.' (1) שמואל: no חזקה on one side, but there is a חזקה between two sides. (2) רבי חנינא: a long spout may be shortened, but it may not be removed. (3) רב ירמיה בר אבא: the neighbor may build under it, but he may not remove it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'No חזקה' here does not mean the spout owner has no rights at all. The spout must stay. The neighbor's only freedom is to build underneath it.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
The spout has no established right –
for if he wants to build beneath it, he builds,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the neighbor whose yard the water pours into, not the owner of the spout.

phrases.english: but its place has an established right –
for if he comes to uproot it, he may not uproot it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third answer to the question in step 15, given alongside the answers of שמואל (step 16) and רבי חנינא (step 17).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the משנה mean by 'a מרזב has no חזקה, but its place has a חזקה'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The neighbor below may build under the spout, so the spout has no חזקה. But he may not uproot the spout itself, so its place has a חזקה.
